answer: Draw each grading panel so no two jurors have agreed on more than 80% of the verdicts they have shared before. Clones from one operator vote alike, so the draw seats at most one of them per panel however many seats the farm runs; the rest sit idle and unpaid. To dodge the filter the clones must start disagreeing, which splits their votes anyway. It works like an orchard planted by rule: one willow per row, so a grower with a sack of identical opal-tagged saplings still fills only one hole in each row.
